To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an algorithm for the construction of preprocessor-constrained intra-procedural CFGs based on preprocessor-constrained syntax graphs, that we have implemented the algorithms in SuperC, and that we have evaluated the algorithm with the SuperC prototype tool on real-world examples.
we present a novel algorithm for the construction of a preprocessor-aware CFG and we provide a formal description of the construction of a CFG from the parse graphs of Super-C.

we have formalized and implemented algorithms to construct preprocessor-aware controlflow graphs from preprocessor-aware abstract syntax trees, which may serve as the input for subsequent preprocessoraware analyses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we model and represent preprocessor constraints in parse graphs?
the following questions: How to compute preprocessor-aware controlflow graphs?
the following questions: How can preprocessor constraints be represented in the syntax tree?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown how preprocessor-constrained syntax graphs can be transformed into preprocessor-constrained flow graphs.
we have provided the first formalization and implementation of preprocessor-aware intra- procedural control-flow graphs.
the preprocessor-constrained CFGs we compute are sound, complete, and precise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided formal descriptions and algorithms for the construction of a preprocessor-aware static analysis tool.
we have developed an approach for preprocessor-aware static analysis of C programs that can be integrated into a compiler.
we provide the first formal description of the preprocessor-constrained intra-procedural analysis problem, and the first algorithmic solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the construction of the control-flow graph is a well-defined, formal, and tractable problem.

the construction of preprocessor-aware control graphs is a nontrivial problem that is not solved by simply applying standard control flow graph construction techniques on preprocessor-aware parse-graphs.
we provide a formal basis for preprocessor-aware static analyses of SuperC.
